title: One stacked-row layout
assertion: Each stacked row is an item of a list named by its label or by the title that names it, a list by its role too (Safari drops the role of an unstyled list), headed by its naming cell at the level the caller gives (h3 by default; a link when the row has one), then, when given, a line that describes it, then a definition list of each column's label and value, terms over values until the list is 24rem wide and beside them after, in a term column of at most 40% of the list, each pair apart from the next in either layout, then the row's actions, with no actions box when they render nothing; expected, paid and short are given together and in that order, and the stacked rows keep the table's column order, each figure, code and count in the mono face with tabular numerals; a status chip, a Badge and a key longer than the card wrap inside it; the rows carry their own hooks, never the table's, and no id or hook repeats between the two copies; with a table, the table shows from the table's own width up and the rows below it, by a container query on a full-width wrapper that is never squeezed to nothing; a list with no name is refused
noFileReason: The stacked rows are rendered from synthetic rows the test passes in memory; no file.
